title: Building DEAD SIGNAL ONLINE with AI assistance: expanding crafting without breaking existing characters
author: raranon
selftext:
I’m developing DEAD SIGNAL ONLINE, a Korean-language 2D online action RPG set in ruined Seoul. I use generative AI for visual assets and assistance with code and text, with developer direction, integration, and testing. This is my own project, and this post is both a development write-up and an introduction to the free online alpha.



A recent update expanded a rifle progression prototype into fourteen equipment families and forty-two crafting targets. The harder part was keeping existing characters compatible: old rifle research and equipment IDs needed to remain valid, while new modifications needed tradeoffs rather than being automatic upgrades. The implementation kept the existing progression curve and added optional growth fields instead of resetting players.



The useful AI workflow was to turn those constraints into explicit checks, then test crafting, dismantling, duplicate requests, and save compatibility against isolated databases before release. Generated code still needed review against the actual save format. Those checks cover specific behavior; they don’t prove that the long-term economy is balanced. That remains a progression playtesting problem. For other developers using AI on persistent games, where have you found the best balance between compatibility checks and longer progression playtests?



The alpha has shared hunting areas, scheduled assaults with a staging phase, and a twelve-floor dungeon. It is free, online-only, and currently Korean-language. The itch.io page includes the Windows launcher, real gameplay screenshots, controls, and AI-use disclosure: https://ddackshow9921-crypto.itch.io/dead-signal-online



Official website and browser access: [https://ds.ggm.kr/](https://ds.ggm.kr/)
